jurisdiction.name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
jurisdiction.overview: Intergovernmental organisation of 38 member countries. Its AI Recommendation is open to non-members, so it applies to its Adherents rather than to OECD membership.

narrative.summary: The OECD Council adopted the Recommendation on Artificial Intelligence in 2019, the first intergovernmental standard on AI, and revised it in November 2023 (definition of an AI system) and May 2024. The OECD has since issued implementation guidance in its own name, including a companion document on data access and sharing in the age of AI and due diligence guidance for responsible AI for enterprises. The Global Partnership on AI, launched in 2020 and integrated with the OECD in 2024, has adopted ministerial declarations in Tokyo (2022), New Delhi (2023, 2024) and Belgrade (2024).
narrative.review_notes: The OECD Compendium of Legal Instruments was searched for AI-specific instruments and only the AI Recommendation was found; adherents and adherence dates are taken from the instrument's page. Membership (38) is taken from the same site's country list, which marks each country as a Member.

instruments.official_title: Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (OECD/LEGAL/0449)
instruments.current_status: In force. Adopted by the OECD Council at Ministerial level on 22 May 2019 and revised on 8 November 2023 and 3 May 2024; it applies to its Adherents (OECD Members and non-member adherents).
instruments.summary: Sets five values-based principles for trustworthy AI and five recommendations to governments on investment, enabling ecosystems, policy environment, skills and international co-operation. The Council revised the definition of an AI system on 8 November 2023 and revised the text on 3 May 2024 to address safety, misinformation and disinformation, environmental sustainability, and to move traceability and risk management under the accountability principle.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Intergovernmental AI principles adhered to by 50 countries and the EU; basis for the G20 AI Principles and the G7 Hiroshima Process texts.
instruments.evidence_reference: Research pass 2026-10-21: Corrections to existing record: (1) legal_status should be nonbinding_recommendation per the spec (OECD Council Recommendation), currently nonbinding_guidance; (2) add 2023-11-08 revision (updated AI system definition; DPC approved draft 16 Oct 2023, Council adopted 8 Nov 2023) alongside last_amended_date 2024-05-03. Read via legalinstruments.oecd.org/api/instruments/OECD-LEGAL-0449 on 2026-10-21; change history also lists 2024-01-07 with no description (linked to the 2024 Report to Council). Adherent count in API data: 51 countries. | Independent check 2026-10-21: corrected from the official source.

instruments.english_title: Enhancing Access to and Sharing of Data in the Age of Artificial Intelligence (Companion Document to the OECD Recommendation on Enhancing Access to and Sharing of Data)
instruments.issuing_authority: OECD Digital Policy Committee, with the Committee for Scientific and Technological Policy and the Public Governance Committee
instruments.publisher_name: OECD Digital Policy Committee, with the Committee for Scientific and Technological Policy and the Public Governance Committee
instruments.summary: Implementation guidance for Adherents and other data ecosystem actors on applying the 2021 OECD Recommendation on Enhancing Access to and Sharing of Data, focused on how AI developments affect data access and sharing. It explains key concepts and illustrates the Recommendation's principles with public and private sector examples.
instruments.current_status: Approved and declassified by the OECD Digital Policy Committee, with the Committee for Scientific and Technological Policy and the Public Governance Committee, on 21 November 2024. Non-binding guidance accompanying a Council Recommendation.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF read 2026-10-21 via WebFetch: cover date 5 February 2025; approval note quoted (DPC with CSTP and PGC, 21 November 2024). Linked from the 0463 instrument page (API). Recorded because it is committee-approved implementation guidance whose main subject is AI; the parent Recommendation 0463 itself is a lead (AI only in background).

instruments.official_title: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible AI
instruments.english_title: OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible AI
instruments.issuing_authority: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
instruments.publisher_name: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
instruments.summary: Practical guidance for enterprises on applying the OECD standards on responsible business conduct and the OECD AI Principles when developing and using AI. It sets out a due diligence process to identify, prevent, mitigate and account for adverse impacts across the AI value chain and seeks alignment with other national and international AI risk management frameworks.
instruments.current_status: Published by the OECD on 19 February 2026 as practical guidance for enterprises.
instruments.evidence_reference: Date 19 February 2026 from the OECD publication page's date field (read via WebFetch, which reported it in the page metadata block; visible text not rendered). PDF blocked by robots for WebFetch, so approving committee not confirmed; check foreword for the approval note (likely Working Party on RBC / Investment Committee and DPC). If the editor prefers printed dates only, set to 2026-02. Australian NCP page says it was released at the India AI Impact Summit 2026. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 19 Feb 2026 date and description confirmed.; Page does not describe the guidance as 'non-binding'.

instruments.official_title: Joint Statement from founding members of the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: Joint Statement from Founding Members of the Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.summary: Launches the Global Partnership on AI (GPAI), an international multistakeholder initiative to guide the responsible development and use of AI, grounded in human rights, inclusion, diversity, innovation and economic growth, and in line with the OECD AI Recommendation. Experts work on responsible AI, data governance, the future of work, and innovation and commercialisation, and on AI in the COVID-19 response.
instruments.current_status: Joint statement of the GPAI founding members (Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico, New Zealand, the Republic of Korea, Singapore, Slovenia, the United Kingdom, the United States and the European Union), published 15 June 2020; the GPAI Secretariat is hosted by the OECD.
instruments.evidence_reference: Published date 15 June 2020 as printed on GOV.UK (founding member government). Same text on canada.ca (ISED news 2020/06) and soumu.go.jp. GPAI had no own site carrying the text; OECD.AI GPAI declarations page starts at 2022. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 15 June 2020, founding members and content confirmed on gov.uk (an official government host). The statement notes the EU's accession was still in progress.; 'Political commitment, not legally binding' is not printed in the statement.

instruments.summary: GPAI ministers meeting in Tokyo recommit to the human-centric values of the OECD AI Recommendation and oppose unlawful and irresponsible uses of AI. They pledge to strengthen GPAI as a multistakeholder initiative, fund its secretariat and project pool, deepen co-operation with the OECD and UNESCO, and implement the 2023 work plan under India's incoming chair.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the Ministers of GPAI Members in Tokyo on 22 November 2022. Political declaration.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF read 2026-10-21; declaration states ministers convened in Tokyo on 21 and 22 November 2022; date taken as 22 November 2022 as printed.

instruments.official_title: Global Partnership on Artificial Intelligence (GPAI) 2023 Ministerial Declaration
instruments.summary: GPAI ministers recommit to safe, secure and trustworthy AI grounded in democratic values, human rights and the OECD AI Recommendation, and to advancing safe AI in their jurisdictions. They aim to widen equitable access to compute and data, build capacity in low- and middle-income countries, add sustainable agriculture as a thematic priority, co-ordinate with the G7, G20, OECD and UNESCO, and broaden membership.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by the GPAI Ministerial Council at its fifth meeting on 13 December 2023 in New Delhi; the declaration is dated 14 December 2023. Political declaration.
instruments.evidence_reference: Read one.oecd.org GPAI(2023)2 on 2026-10-21; also on wp.oecd.ai/app/uploads/2025/01/2023-GPAI-Ministerial-Declaration.pdf. | Independent check 2026-10-21: corrected from the official source.

instruments.summary: Sets a renewed vision for GPAI as an integrated partnership with the OECD, placing OECD members and GPAI countries on an equal footing under the GPAI brand on the basis of the OECD AI Recommendation. Members decide new memberships, observers and work priorities by consensus; governance runs through a Council, Plenary and Steering Group, and the GPAI and OECD expert groups merge into one expert community.
instruments.current_status: Adopted by GPAI Ministers in New Delhi on 3-4 July 2024. Political declaration.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF prints '3-4 July 2024' (meeting dates) with no single signature date; month given only.

instruments.summary: GPAI ministers, building on the 2024 New Delhi Declaration's integrated partnership with the OECD, commit to evidence-based joint work on AI and employment, data governance, intellectual property and bridging global AI divides, and to welcoming new members, including developing and emerging economies.
instruments.current_status: Adopted at the GPAI Summit in Belgrade, 3-4 December 2024, under the co-chairmanship of Serbia and the Slovak Republic; dated 4 December 2024.
instruments.evidence_reference: PDF read 2026-10-21; dated 4 December 2024. | Independent check 2026-10-21: Title, 4 Dec 2024, Belgrade, GPAI Summit 3-4 Dec 2024, Serbia and Slovak Republic as Co-Chairs and summary content confirmed.; 'Political declaration' not printed; Serbia and Slovakia are described as Co-Chairs rather than co-leads of the summit.
